title: 4-to-1 Multiplexer: Two Select Bits Pick a Wire
topic: 4-to-1 multiplexer — four data inputs (D0..D3) and two select inputs (S1, S0) feed into a logic block that routes whichever input is addressed by the select bits to a single output Y; demonstrates how 2^n select bits address 2^n data lines

beats.narration: Four wires want to share one output line — how do we pick which one talks?

elements.content: Manimo enters centre-screen
Four signals, one output — who gets through?

beats.narration: A four to one multiplexer: four data inputs on the left, two select bits at the bottom, and a single output on the right.

elements.content: Trapezoidal MUX block in the centre
Four input wires D0..D3 stub on the left edge
Two select wires S1, S0 entering the bottom of the block
Single output wire Y leaving the right tip
Labels D0, D1, D2, D3 next to input wires
S1, S0 labels under the select inputs
Y label at the output
two bits address four lines

beats.narration: Walk the select bits from zero zero up to one one. Whichever input is addressed lights up, and its signal walks through the block to the output.

elements.content: Active path: the addressed input wire glows amber and a charge dot travels through the MUX to Y
Live S1 S0 readout above the select wires, ticking through four states
Live Y readout near the output, showing whichever Di is currently selected
Truth-table row at the bottom highlighting the active row
select bits decode to one of four enable lines

beats.narration: In Boolean form, Y is the OR of four AND terms: each data line ANDed with the decoded address that selects it.

elements.content: only the matching AND term is non-zero — the rest are silenced

beats.narration: A multiplexer is a programmable switch — and chaining them lets one address space pick from many more lines.

elements.content: An addressable switch.
the same idea scales — n select bits address 2^n lines
